clue.text: Joint interest about pound

indicators.note: about says the word for interest wraps round the pound sign

parts.note: spice is what adds interest or zest, as in 'variety is the spice of life'
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A remark about the interest earned on a pound in a shared venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like a shared account but is the definition; 'about' puts L inside SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A splice is a join, especially where two ropes or film strips are woven or glued together.

clue.text: Tame reminder from membership secretary?

parts.note: a membership secretary reminds members their subscription (sub) is due
a membership secretary reminds members their subscription (sub) is due

explanation.surface: A gentle reminder notice from a club's membership secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the reading 'sub due', the subscription reminder a club sends.
explanation.definitionFit: To tame an animal or person is to subdue them, bringing them under control.

clue.text: Reading rooms that make houses share article

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac, which astrologers call houses

indicators.note: share says the two words overlap on one letter, so the second loses its copy

parts.note: Aries is another zodiac sign, or house
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Reading rooms that make neighbouring houses split an article between them.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBRA and ARIES overlap on their shared A, so the second's A drops out. 'Reading' is not the English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are rooms or buildings where people go to read and borrow books.

clue.text: For whom decline follows hype, could one say?

definitions.text: For whom decline follows hype, could one say?

indicators.note: could one say signals that the pieces are spoken to give the answer's sound

parts.note: hype is a hard sell, and decline is an ebb, so ebb follows sell

explanation.surface: Asking about someone whose fall comes right after the hype.
explanation.walkthrough: SELL followed by EBB, said aloud, gives the answer. The whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity often rises on hype and then fades from view, the fate the clue describes.

clue.text: Sherman, for example, very nearly rolling into a base

indicators.note: into says the shortened word goes inside the word for base

parts.note: base means mean or low, as in base motives

indicators.note: very nearly says the last letter of the word for rolling is lost

parts.note: rolling (in it) means very rich

explanation.surface: A Sherman tank lumbers almost all the way into a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very nearly' trims RICH to RIC, which goes 'into' A MEAN. 'Rolling' looks like movement, but it means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: General Sherman and the Sherman tank are both American, so either is an example of one.

clue.text: Able to dynamite crumbling old defence works

indicators.note: crumbling says the letters of the phrase fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone able to blow up a ruined old fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' rearranges ABLE TO DYNAMITE. A motte-and-bailey was a Norman castle on a mound with a walled courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A motte-and-bailey castle is an early medieval fortification, a mound with an enclosed yard.

clue.text: Dog on journey not finishing at any time

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: not finishing says the word for journey loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a journey
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A dog on a never-ending walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts TRIP to TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a breed of gun dog, such as the golden or Labrador.

clue.text: Wire in the centre reached up to it

indicators.note: in the centre picks out the middle letter of reached

parts.note: able means capable, up to it

explanation.surface: A wire in the middle reached as far as it could.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of the seven-letter REACHED is C. 'Wire' as a noun means a telegram, as does cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a thick wire, or a telegram, which was also once called a wire.

clue.text: Approaches fish horseman's left

parts.note: nears means approaches
an ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A rider approaches a fish on the left side of the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The nearside of a horse is its left side, from which a rider traditionally mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsemen call the left side of a horse the nearside, the side they mount from.

clue.text: Urban myths led to blunder about hard music

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the hard letter
to blunder says the words are jumbled clumsily into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Urban myths lead people to blunder about tough music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to blunder' rearranges URBAN MYTHS LED, and that goes 'about' H.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythm and blues is a style of popular music that grew out of African American blues.

clue.text: Hope wool producer's sound, keeping husband in knitwear

parts.note: Bob Hope was the comedian, so Hope suggests his first name

indicators.note: keeping says the sheep's cry holds the husband inside it

parts.note: a sheep is the wool producer and its sound is a bleat

explanation.surface: Hoping a sheep sounds healthy while a husband stays tucked in a woolly garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' is the comedian Bob Hope, so it gives BOB. A BOBBLE HAT is a knitted woolly hat with a pompom on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted woolly cap with a pompom is a classic item of knitwear.

clue.text: Lying back in herbal bath, that has stretched skin

indicators.note: Lying back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reclining in a herbal bath, skin wrinkled and stretched.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run ALBAT, read backwards, gives the answer. A TABLA is an Indian hand drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabla is an Indian drum whose playing surface is animal hide stretched taut over the shell.

clue.text: Name of satellite with no sides

indicators.note: with no sides says the first and last letters of the word come off

parts.note: lunar means relating to the moon, Earth's satellite

explanation.surface: Asking what a satellite with no side panels is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of satellite' is the adjective LUNAR; losing its sides leaves the girl's name UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Una is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Unusual interest in public transport, being rich

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the word interest are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes an odd interest in buses because they are wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges INTEREST to UTTERINES, which goes 'in' BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Butteriness is richness, the quality of food being full of fat, like butter.

clue.text: Friends, for example, lie and tease endlessly

parts.note: to sit is to lie or rest in place, as a book sits on a shelf

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for tease is dropped

parts.note: to tease hair is to comb it out

explanation.surface: Friends sometimes lie to and tease one another without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends is the American TV comedy series, not a set of companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The TV series Friends is a famous example of a situation comedy.

clue.text: It blends in tea with fruit containing tip of camomile

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: containing says the fruit holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a melon is a fruit

indicators.note: tip of picks the end letter of camomile

explanation.surface: Something that blends into a cup of tea and fruit with a dash of camomile.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tip' here is the final letter of CAMOMILE, E. 'It blends in' looks like the tea but describes the lizard's camouflage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon lizard changes colour to match its surroundings, so it blends in.

clue.text: Agreement about travel document for Serbian town

indicators.note: about says the word for agreement goes round the travel document

parts.note: a nod is a sign of agreement
a visa is a document that allows entry to a country

explanation.surface: Getting the nod on a visa application for a trip to Serbia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreement' looks like a pact but is a nod of the head. NOVI SAD is Serbia's second city, on the Danube.
explanation.definitionFit: Novi Sad is a large city in northern Serbia, capital of Vojvodina province.

clue.text: Fixed increases bound to get market going

parts.note: set means fixed, as in a set price
ups are increases, as in ups and downs
to hop is to bound or leap

explanation.surface: Fixed rises in price are bound to get a market moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. To set up shop is to start in business.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up shop is to start trading, which gets a market stall going.

clue.text: One's put on no end of weight drinking tawny port

indicators.note: drinking says the pair of pieces takes the colour word inside
put on says the first piece sits on top of the second in this down entry

parts.note: One's is I's, read as one is

indicators.note: no end of says the last letter of the word for weight goes

parts.note: bulk is weight or mass
tan is a tawny colour

explanation.surface: Someone piling on weight from drinking tawny port.
explanation.walkthrough: IS put on BUL gives ISBUL, which takes in TAN. 'port' is a harbour city, not wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is a major Turkish seaport on the Bosphorus, so it is a port.

clue.text: Mark keeps place for 4 in hold up

indicators.note: keeps says the mark holds the country inside it

parts.note: a stain is a mark
4 across names a nationality whose country is the US

explanation.surface: A mark stays put on the place set aside for someone in a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place for 4' means the country of 4 across's people, the US. The clue's 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to support it or hold it up, as pillars sustain a roof.

clue.text: Blackleg infiltrating Labour Party slate

indicators.note: infiltrating says the strikebreaker gets inside the gathering

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for shared work, like a sewing bee
a rat is a blackleg, a worker who breaks a strike

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker infiltrates the Labour Party to slate its policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour Party' is not the political party but a BEE, a working party. 'slate' is a verb meaning criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise them severely, which is what berating does.

clue.text: African range don't agree to climb

parts.note: ken is range of knowledge or sight, as in beyond my ken

indicators.note: to climb says the word goes upwards, read backwards in a down entry

parts.note: nay is a vote of no, saying you don't agree

explanation.surface: Mountaineers argue about climbing an African range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like mountains but means KEN, range of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya, an East African country.

clue.text: First-rate times had by male graduate in Southern French town

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the top grade, written here with I for the digit one
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
Les is a man's name, short for Leslie, so it stands for a male
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A male graduate down south has a wonderful time in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had by' is a link. 'male' giving LES, a man's name, is loose; the 'in' is taken literally. AIX-LES-BAINS is a spa town in Savoie.
explanation.definitionFit: Aix-les-Bains is a spa resort in the Savoie region of south-eastern France.

clue.text: Expel bleach regularly in old vessel

indicators.note: regularly picks out every second letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Ejecting bleach from an old ship at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: A XEBEC is a small three-masted Mediterranean sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A xebec is a three-masted sailing ship once used in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Rocks put on box dropping down finally

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let go from the word

parts.note: to screen a show is to put it on the box, television

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of down

explanation.surface: Rocks dropped onto a box finally fall down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is TV slang; SCREEN loses N, the end of 'down'. Scree is loose broken rock on a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is the mass of loose fallen rocks at the foot of a cliff or slope.

clue.text: Rook perhaps avoiding church where blackbirds sang

indicators.note: avoiding says the church's letters are left out

parts.note: a rook is an example of a chess piece
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rook steers clear of the church where blackbirds sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' is the chess piece, not the bird. The definition is the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence, where four and twenty blackbirds baked in a pie began to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, blackbirds are baked in a pie and sing when it is opened.

clue.text: Anger that bachelor has stopped getting reliable work

indicators.note: has stopped says the bachelor plugs a gap inside the word for anger

parts.note: bile means bad temper or anger

explanation.surface: An angry man whose bachelorhood ended and who now has steady work.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside BILE. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible is often called the authoritative book, a work trusted as true by believers.

clue.text: Mysterious Lutheran works close to blasphemy

indicators.note: works says the letters of Lutheran are worked into a new order
close to picks the last letter of blasphemy

explanation.surface: A Lutheran's writings come mysteriously near to blasphemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun for writings but tells you to rearrange LUTHERAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthly means unnatural or eerie, as if from another world, so mysterious.

clue.text: Volume has chapter for second couple's reputedly monstrous scene

indicators.note: for second couple's says chapter takes the place of the third and fourth letters

parts.note: loudness is volume of sound

explanation.surface: A book volume with a chapter on a pair of famous monster sightings.
explanation.walkthrough: In LOUDNESS the second pair of letters is UD; CH replaces it. 'has' is a link. Loch Ness is a Scottish lake said to be home to a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Loch Ness in Scotland is famous as the reputed home of a monster, Nessie.

clue.text: Move smartly to catch rebounding skittle

indicators.note: rebounding says the two words bounce back and are read backwards

parts.note: to nip is to move quickly, as in nip to the shops
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: Darting in to catch a skittle that bounces back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebounding' reverses NIPNET as a whole to give TENPIN. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenpin is one of the ten skittles knocked down in bowling.
